A curve has equation $3e^{3x}y+y^2=-2$. The point $P=(0,-1)$ lies on the curve.

Show that $y\prime=-\frac{9e^{3x}y}{3e^{3x}+2y}$ where the denominator is nonzero, showing all necessary working.

marking_memo.grading_guide_answer:
Part show-derivative
$y\prime=-\frac{9e^{3x}y}{3e^{3x}+2y}$
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:show-derivative:S1 [1]: Attempt a complete differentiation of the product (or an approved equivalent relation), allowing one numerical slip but no omitted contribution.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:show-derivative:S2 [1]: Correct exponential/product/composite differentiation on the selected valid route.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:show-derivative:S3 [1]: Correct remaining implicit derivative and constant zero; on the explicit-root route justify the root/y identity.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:show-derivative:S4 [1]: Complete correct forward derivation establishes the supplied target or a demonstrated equivalent; all preceding proof evidence is correct and complete. No follow-through into the supplied result.
Differentiate the exponential product — Both factors depend on x; include the exponential chain factor. — $9e^{3x}y+3e^{3x}y\prime$
Differentiate the remaining terms — y depends on x; the right-hand side is constant. — $\frac{d}{dx}(y^2)=2yy\prime$, $\frac{dC}{dx}=0$
Collect terms containing the derivative — Isolate the requested derivative by forward algebra. — $(3e^{3x}+2y)y\prime=-9e^{3x}y$
Divide by the nonzero coefficient — The expression is valid on a local branch where the denominator is nonzero. — $y\prime=-\frac{9e^{3x}y}{3e^{3x}+2y}$

Part gradient
$9$
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:gradient:H1 [1]: Substitute the point into the displayed derivative or a credible derivative from the proof, respecting hence.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:gradient:H2 [1]: Canonical exact or 3 s.f. gradient after valid substitution; no ordinary final-accuracy follow-through.
Substitute the supplied point — Use the derivative at P, keeping exact arithmetic. — $m=-\frac{(3)(3)(-1)}{3+2(-1)}=9$

Part normal
$y=-\frac{1}{9}x - 1$
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:normal:N1 [1]: Show or state a labelled perpendicular gradient equal to minus the reciprocal of their credible finite nonzero tangent gradient.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:normal:N2 [1]: Construct the line through the supplied point using their perpendicular gradient; limited method follow-through.
WB8227-implicit-normal@0.1.4:normal:normal:N3 [1]: Canonical exact normal in any equivalent line form after visible normal working; ordinary final accuracy is not follow-through.
Find the perpendicular gradient — A finite nonzero tangent gradient has perpendicular gradient minus its reciprocal. — $m_\perp=-\frac{1}{9}=-\frac{1}{9}$
Construct the line through P — Use point-gradient form with the perpendicular gradient. — $y-(-1)=-\frac{1}{9}(x-0)$
Simplify the equation — Equivalent exact affine forms describe the same line. — $y=-\frac{1}{9}x - 1$

`workbench/playbook/guidelines/provenance.json` (7 November 2026, file digests pinned
in the planning manifest). Those were local app snapshots, not proof of deployed
bytes. No forked shared AI instruction is added. Use British spelling, clear

as learner copy. Render all later question, help, solution, feedback and history
surfaces; a tolerant formatter does not establish authoring compliance.

an action/reason/result repair. It distinguishes an ambiguous upload from a wrong
answer, and the app retains the original attempt. No invented misconception is
labelled examiner-evidenced. Solutions/support and ordinary practice do not move
memory boxes; the application owns reliable completed-test progress.
